faqs.q: Can TPO be installed on a flat-roofed two-family home or garden apartment in Bloomfield?

runs.v: Yes: TPO is a flexible membrane suited to them, and Bloomfield homeowners get tapered insulation, welded seams, and new parapet flashing.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a TPO roof on a Bloomfield commercial building?

runs.v: Usually: TPO roofing work follows the NJ Uniform Construction Code, and the 25% rule in N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 requires a permit for work over 25% of the roof in 12 months on commercial, multi-family, or attached buildings.

faqs.q: Does TPO installation on a Bloomfield Center historic property need extra approval?

runs.v: It can: historic-district properties can need extra review, so confirm with the township construction office.

faqs.q: How long does a TPO roof last on a Bloomfield building?

runs.v: 7 to 20 years per InterNACHI, and properly installed TPO systems are often cited at 20 to 30 years; yearly checks add long-term protection and long-lasting performance.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a reflective white TPO roof and a dark membrane?

runs.v: White TPO is energy efficient: its reflective surface reflects sunlight, cutting cooling loads, energy costs, and urban heat islands, unlike a heat-absorbing dark membrane; TPO is often called 100% recyclable, with no chlorine or plasticizers.
